A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ViP2-CLIP work, and their main text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. However, v1 includes Appendices A–D, whereas v2 references Appendices A–C but ends after its references. The unavailable later appendices limit comparison and do not establish that their experiments were deleted.

before.justification: V1 reports original anomaly detection and segmentation results across 15 benchmarks, component ablations, and additional experimental analyses in its appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains the original benchmark results and reports additional component combinations, a controlled alignment comparison, and layer-dependent anomaly maps.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 retain the same ICA conditioning, FGP attention, Top-k text-patch alignment, training losses and multilayer inference procedure. The new alignment experiments test existing components rather than change the proposed method.

E1.justification: The main evaluations retain the same seven industrial and eight medical datasets and detection/localization tasks. V1 additionally documents medical auxiliary-data training and class-name perturbation scenarios in its appendices; their status cannot be established because v2's referenced appendices are unavailable.

E2.justification: V2 Table 5 adds an explicit CLIP_DUAL comparison against CLIP_UTPA to test alignment strategies. The five main ZSAD baselines and efficiency comparators remain unchanged. Whether v1's appendix comparison with PatchCore and RD4AD remains in the later work cannot be verified.

E3.justification: V2 expands the component experiment from four configurations to seven and adds a frozen-CLIP, learnable-prompt control comparing dual-branch alignment with UTPA. The efficiency evaluation also reports GPU memory and trainable parameter counts. The documented main backbone, cross-dataset training/testing arrangement and accuracy metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 substantially broadens component analysis: Table 4 adds FGP-only and additional UTPA combinations, Table 5 isolates alignment strategy, and Figure 7 examines localization across network depths. The existing adjective and Top-k studies remain. These additions test component interactions and alignment behavior beyond v1's cumulative ablation; appendix-only analyses cannot be compared completely.

E5.justification: The inference-time values and their ± quantities are identical in v1 Table 7 and v2 Table 3. Neither supplied PDF explains these quantities through run counts or a specified uncertainty estimator. The additional ablation results introduce no new seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2, the adjective-ablation results, original component rows and timing measurements are unchanged. V2 adds targeted ablation results, resource measurements and layer-dependent findings. In the new Table 5, CLIP_DUAL versus CLIP_UTPA yields MVTec pixel AUROC of 69.6 versus 89.6, but image AUROC of 88.6 versus 85.0; this is a new controlled comparison, not an improvement over v1's headline performance. Appendix-only results remain unverified.

T1.justification: V1's explicit binary-softmax equation, Eq. 7, is replaced by a reference to the equivalent probability definition in v2 Eq. 1. The remaining mathematical procedure is equivalent despite renumbering. No substantive definitions, derivations, assumptions or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same visual-conditioned, class-name-independent prompting and unified-alignment contributions, together with the same 15-benchmark performance and cross-domain generalization claims. Additional supporting analyses do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explanation linking negative image-level F1 gains on BTAD and DAGM to domain shifts affecting ICA, interprets layer-dependent localization, and develops the optimization-conflict argument for UTPA. V1's explicit qualification about dataset-specific optimal Top-k selection and its privacy caveat have no counterpart in the readable v2 text.

D1.justification: V2 changes the reported NVIDIA L20 capacity from 42 to 48 GB, identifies VisA for the efficiency comparison, and adds memory and parameter counts. However, v1 Appendix B supplies Adam, learning rate 0.001, 10 epochs, batch size 8, image preprocessing and baseline implementation details; v2 points to an unavailable Appendix B. Whether these details or underlying settings were retained or revised cannot be determined.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds MMRL by Guo and Gu alongside multimodal prompt-learning work. V2's reference list omits the PatchCore and RD4AD papers cited in v1's appendix comparison. Positioning against the main CLIP-based methods remains substantially unchanged; the switch to numbered citations is stylistic.

P1.justification: The six main sections and much of their wording remain. V2 shortens the opening motivation in Section 4.1, revises the prompt-learning paragraph and experimental discussion, and moves the expanded efficiency discussion into the main text. Author affiliations and contribution markers also change; the standalone limitations and ethics sections are absent.

P2.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the visual presentation through a different page format and resized or relocated figures, including moving Figure 1 into a first-page column. It moves and expands the appendix efficiency table, replaces cumulative module labels with an explicit component matrix, and adds the alignment-comparison table and layer-visualization figure. Retained Figures 1–5 reuse the same images.

improvement.justification: V2's expanded controls, layer analysis and resource measurements provide useful additional evidence while retaining the main results. However, its stronger UTPA interpretation only partly acknowledges the detection/localization tradeoff in Table 5. The unavailable referenced appendices also prevent checking important implementation details and supporting evidence present in v1. These gains, qualifications and material gaps prevent a reliable overall quality judgment.
